Medusa. Once a beautiful woman transformed into a horrifying monster with serpents for hair, Medusa possessed the terrifying power to turn anyone who looked upon her into stone. Her hair consisted of living venomous snakes that constantly writhed and hissed, replacing the golden locks she once had. A single glance into her eyes could instantly petrify any living creature, freezing them in stone for eternity.

She was cursed or transformed by Athena after being violated by Poseidon in one of the goddess's own temples. Before her transformation, she was the only mortal among the three Gorgon sisters—Stheno and Euryale were immortal. She lived in a cavern far to the west, beyond the land of the Hyperboreans, in a place of desolation and stone. The young hero Perseus defeated her by using a polished bronze shield as a mirror, avoiding her deadly gaze while he struck. Her severed head retained its petrifying power even in death, and Perseus mounted it on his shield as protection in his future battles. Some accounts describe her as a victim of circumstance rather than a true monster, transformed against her will.
